one_month_reasoning: There is no Broadcom report in the window: it reports Q4 FY26 after the close on Wed 2026-12-09 [2], after 2026-11-05. Events in the window are all in the industry. TSMC Q3 results come on 2026-10-15 [14]. In July TSMC called packaging capacity so tight it limits customers' growth [13], so this print is a supply read-through, two-sided. The big hyperscalers report in late October (exact dates not confirmed), the first chance at numeric 2027 capex guides. Every 2026 guide from Alphabet, Meta and Amazon went up [11]; Alphabet, Broadcom's TPU customer, raised to $195-205B from $180-190B in July [18]. So the skew is mildly positive, but that is widely expected. Today's +4% came alongside Marvell's investor day (MRVL +7.5% per Investing.com [15]; event confirmed by Marvell IR [16]). That is read-through, not Broadcom news, and after a fast run a partial reversal is about as likely as follow-through. I use a near-symmetric lognormal: median $379 (slight drift) and monthly sigma 13.5% (47%/3.5), with 15% weight on a 1.6x-sigma component for fat tails. P(>=377.32) = 0.51.

fair_value.method: Estimate. 0.7 x P/E $472 (my FY28 EPS $23.60, built on FY28 AI $180B, total revenue $232B, 61% operating margin, x 20x, inside the 15.3-59.8x CY2027 peer range) + 0.3 x DCF $318 (FY28 FCF/share $19.70 at 0.835 conversion; growth 15/10/6/4%, terminal 3%, 10.5% discount) = $425.9 -> $426.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28 EPS $23.60 x 20x. FY28 revenue $232B = AI $180B + non-AI semis $17.2B + software $34.8B; op margin 61%; net interest/other $2.72B; tax 16%; 4.94B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Three cross-checks. (a) Purchase commitments: my FY27 revenue build $167.0B (AI $115B [2] + non-AI $17.2B + software $34.8B) / FY27 commitments $52.674B [4] = 3.170x; x FY28 commitments $72.952B [4] = $231.3B total, less $17.2B and $34.8B = $179.3B AI. (b) Same on semis only: ($115B + $17.2B) / $52.674B = 2.510x; x $72.952B = $183.1B, less $17.2B = $165.9B AI. (c) Share of house 2028 base AI capex $2,255B [11]: FY27 $115B is 6.25% of 2027 base $1,841B [11]; +2pt for the GW ramp (Anthropic +10 GW and OpenAI >5 GW in 2028 vs +5 GW and 1.3 GW in 2027 [2]) = 8.2% x 2,255 = $185B. Band $166-185B; I use $180B (8.0% of 2028 base capex). Note the FY28 commitment bucket was flat over the quarter ($72.870B at 2026-05-03 [5] vs $72.952B at 2026-08-02 [4]), so I do not assume late orders lift it. Management's $230B line of sight [2] is the bull case.
Q4 FY26 guide ~$4.3B [2] x 4 = $17.2B, held flat (no growth assumed).
Q4 FY26 guide ~$8.7B [2] x 4 = $34.8B, held flat.

Q3: AI $16.7B of $29.591B revenue = 56.4% AI mix at 67.9% op margin ($20,095M / $29,591M) [1]; Q4 guide: AI $21.7B of $34.8B = 62.4% mix at ~66% [1][2]. Slope -1.9pt margin per +6.0pt AI mix = -0.317. FY28 mix 77.6% (+15.2pt vs Q4) -> -4.8pt -> 61.2%, rounded to 61%. Consistent with non-GAAP GM falling from 75.0% in Q3 ($22,191M / $29,591M [1]) to ~73% guided for Q4 [2].
Q3 interest expense $778M less other income, net $98M [1] = $680M x 4 = $2.72B, held flat (debt carrying value $2,252M + $57,167M = $59.42B [1]).
Non-GAAP tax rate ~16% [2], held flat. Build check on Q3: ($20,095M - $778M + $98M) x 0.84 = $16,309M vs reported non-GAAP NI $16,372M [1] (-0.4%).
(232.0 x 0.61 - 2.72) x 0.84 / 4.94 = (141.52 - 2.72) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $23.60; +21.7% vs FY27 consensus $19.39 [6]. Management says FY28 EPS will exceed $30 [2]; I do not assume that.

inputs_detail.input: P/E multiple at the Oct-2027 horizon (on NTM = FY28 EPS)
inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median on one CY2027 basis is 26.0x, range 15.3x (NVDA) to 59.8x (ALAB) [7-10]; large-cap (>$400B) cohort NVDA 15.3x, TSM 21.8x, CSCO 21.9x, AMD 40.9x -> median 21.9x [7]; AVGO today 19.5x FY27 ($377.32 / $19.39 [6]). 20x is inside the peer range, ~23% below the median; reasons it persists through the horizon are in comps_summary.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at the Oct-2027 horizon: FY28 FCF/share $19.70 (0.835 x $23.60), growth 15/10/6/4% FY29-32, terminal 3%, discount 10.5% (10-yr 5.31% + 5.2pt)

inputs_detail.derivation: FCF conversion Q3: FCF $13,665M / non-GAAP NI $16,372M [1] = 0.835; x FY28 EPS $23.60 = $19.70.
House base AI capex grows +22% in 2028 (1,841 -> 2,255) [11] and the file gives no 2029+ path; I fade growth below that rate as AI mix matures and the GW ramp [2] laps.
Below the 10-yr nominal Treasury yield 5.31% [12]; a mature-semis/software long-run nominal rate.
10-yr Treasury 5.31% on 2026-10-05 [12] + 5.2pt equity premium for a high-volatility (47% realized, per brief) semiconductor.

inputs_detail.input: DCF value at the Oct-2027 horizon
inputs_detail.derivation: PV at 10.5% of FY28 FCF $19.70 and FY29-32 at 15/10/6/4% growth, plus terminal (FY32 FCF x 1.03 / (0.105 - 0.03)) discounted 5 years = $318 (terminal is 72% of value).

bear.story: AI capex digestion: 2028 capex follows the house low case ($1,265B, below 2027's $1,390B low [11]) and FY28 AI revenue stays ~$110B, about flat on FY27's supply-secured $115B [2]. Revenue $162B, op margin 64% (less AI mix), EPS (162 x 0.64 - 2.72) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $17.17. P/E 14x (the group de-rates; ~9% below today's lowest peer, NVDA 15.3x [7]) = $240, weight 0.7; DCF scaled $318 x 17.17/23.60 = $231, weight 0.3. Blend $237. Customer-financing tail: up to $29B max undiscounted backstop plus a $42B undrawn note facility [3], ~$5.9/share for the backstop alone (29/4.94); not netted, since rack value offsets it.

base.story: FY27 AI ~$115B delivered [2]; FY28 tracks ~$180B, in line with the purchase-commitment ramp (FY28 $73.0B vs FY27 $52.7B [4]) and an 8.0% share of house base 2028 capex [11]. Margins dilute to ~61% on XPU/rack mix; EPS $23.60; 20x NTM blended with the DCF = $426 (= fair value).

bull.story: The full $230B FY28 AI line of sight [2] is underwritten: house high capex ($3,160B in 2028 [11], a 7.3% share). Revenue $282B, op margin 60%, EPS (282 x 0.60 - 2.72) x 0.84 / 4.94 = $28.31. P/E 22x (large-cap peer cohort median 21.9x [7]) = $623, weight 0.7; DCF scaled $318 x 28.31/23.60 = $382, weight 0.3. Blend $550.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E on one CY2027 basis: 15.3x (NVDA) to 59.8x (ALAB). Sorted: 15.3, 17.9, 21.8, 21.9, 25.2, 26.0, 28.3, 40.8, 40.9, 42.5, 59.8; median 26.0x (CRDO). Finviz 'Fwd P/E' uses each company's next fiscal year. For NVDA, MRVL (Jan FYE), QCOM (Sep), ADI (Oct) and TSM/AMD/ANET/ALAB (Dec) that is ~CY2027, but for CSCO, COHR and CRDO it is a fiscal year ending mid-2028, so I calendarized those three (math in each comp). Forward EV/EBITDA is null: no verifiable free source gives it on a consistent basis, and the trailing figures I put in that field in round 1 were mislabelled. Peer median next-FY EPS growth is +49.9% (Finviz).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 20x NTM (FY28) P/E at the horizon: inside the 15.3-59.8x range, ~23% below the 26.0x median, slightly below the 21.9x large-cap cohort median (NVDA 15.3, TSM 21.8, CSCO 21.9, AMD 40.9) and in line with AVGO's own 19.5x on FY27 consensus ($377.32 / $19.39 [6]).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount is to the median only. 20x is inside the peer range, and I rest it on factors that persist through Oct-2027. (1) Growth at the horizon: the market will be capitalising FY28, where my EPS grows +21.7% ($23.60 vs $19.39 FY27 consensus [6]), against a peer median next-FY EPS growth of +49.9% [7]. (2) Concentration: six XPU customers [2], with FY28 growth resting on two lab customers' GW ramps (Anthropic +10 GW, OpenAI >5 GW [2]). (3) Customer financing that lasts beyond the horizon: a 5-year backstop with max undiscounted exposure of $29B plus a $42B uncommitted (undrawn) convertible-note facility to the customer [3]. (4) Gross-margin dilution as AI/rack mix rises (non-GAAP GM 75.0% in Q3 [1] to ~73% Q4 guide [2]). The market already prices the most similar mega-cap AI silicon franchise, NVDA, at 15.3x [7] with higher next-FY growth (+70%), so a large-cap AI discount is observable, not assumed. I claim no premium. Differences with the supervisor: my median is 26.0x, not 23.7x, because its set left CSCO, COHR and CRDO on fiscal years ending mid-2028; I keep the same 11 peers (dropped MU and KLAC, added CSCO and COHR).

thesis_break_reason: $265 is 30% below today and 8.6% below the 52-week low of $289.96. It is 13.7x FY27 consensus EPS of $19.39 [6] and 15.4x my bear-case FY28 EPS of $17.17. A price there would mean the market is pricing the bear world (AI revenue flat at ~$110B in FY28), i.e. that it no longer trusts the supply-secured ~$115B FY27 AI revenue [2] or the FY28 purchase-commitment ramp [4]. Likely triggers: a cut or soft FY27 guide on 2026-12-09, a lab customer deferring GW deployments, a lease default that activates the up-to-$29B backstop [3], or a 2027-28 capex cut toward the house low case [11]. That is a fundamental break, not 47%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 follows the supervisor's findings, each re-checked at the primary source. (1) FY28 AI revenue: I cut my $195B to $180B. Three of my own cross-checks bracket it: scaling the 10-Q purchase commitments (FY27 $52.7B, FY28 $73.0B [4]) gives $179B on total revenue and $166B on semis only; an 8.2% share of house 2028 base capex gives $185B [11]. The FY28 commitment bucket did not grow between the Q2 and Q3 10-Qs [4][5]. (2) I dropped the 'FY27 consensus x 21x' leg: at an Oct-2027 horizon the market prices FY28, and stalled earnings belong in the bear scenario, not at a full multiple. A DCF (30% weight) replaces it, at the verified 10-yr of 5.31% [12] and Q3 FCF conversion of 0.835 [1]. (3) The P/E build is now pinned to reported Q3 lines: interest $778M less other income $98M [1], margin slope from Q3 to the Q4 guide [1][2]; the build reproduces Q3 non-GAAP NI within 0.4%. (4) Peers: 11 names on one CY2027 basis from Finviz, with three off-cycle names calendarized [7-10]; the median is 26.0x, not my old 30.6x (mixed NTM) nor the supervisor's 23.7x (which kept CSCO/COHR/CRDO on mid-2028 fiscal years). I use 20x, inside the range, for the persistent reasons in comps_summary. (5) Removed from every number: the Anthropic S-1 figures, press-reported $60B bank financing, and Marvell's targets (context only [15][16]); the $42B is now cited from Broadcom's 10-Q [3]. I did not use the MS SPCX digest's AVGO EV/EBIT/growth bar-chart value (marked unverified). Industry read: Broadcom's Q3 AI revenue $16.7B [1] vs NVIDIA Data Center $89.0B [17] means ~16% of the pair. TSMC calls packaging the binding constraint [13]. Result: FY28 EPS $23.60, P/E leg $472, DCF $318, fair value $426. Scenarios: bear $237 (25%), base $426 (50%), bull $550 (25%), weighted mean $410. The ladder is a mixture of three lognormals centred on the scenario prices (sigmas 0.36/0.30/0.33, giving overall log-sd ~0.45 vs 47% realized). Its median is ~$408 (P(>=415) 0.48), its mean ~$432, and P(>=377) = 0.57. The fair value of $426 sits between the ladder median and mean; the median is below it because the bear case is further from base than the bull is. I trimmed the right tail (P(>=943) 0.044 -> 0.015). Analyst targets were not used as anchors.
